cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's people scattered across five regions (1 Peter 1:1). He's already told them the old crowd heaps abuse on them for not joining in the wild life anymore (1 Peter 4:4). Now he calls them 'Beloved' and names what they're going through: a fiery trial.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to treat their fiery trial as something strange and unexpected.
Instead of being surprised by the fiery trial, Peter tells the believers to ___.
Peter tells these believers to rejoice in their fiery trial. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Their trial proves their own strength
Their enemies will soon give up

cards.text: And sharing in His sufferings now leads somewhere: being OVERJOYED when His glory is revealed. Then Peter gets specific about one kind of suffering, being insulted for the name of Christ.

cards.question: Peter says a believer who is insulted for the name of Christ is blessed.
Why does Peter call the believer who is insulted for Christ's name blessed?

answers.text: The Spirit of glory rests on them
The angels of heaven guard them
Their insulters will be struck down

cards.text: Now Peter draws a line: none of them should suffer as a murderer, a thief, a wrongdoer, or even a meddler. MEDDLER made the same list as MURDERER, friend, and I can't walk past a baker's mixing bowl without poking my mustache in, so I'm feeling REAL called out.

cards.question: But if a believer suffers as a Christian, Peter says not to be ___, and to glorify God for bearing that name.

cards.text: Then Peter says something that makes me set down the cookie box I'm packing and stand up REAL straight. It's time, he says, for judgment to begin, and it begins with the family of God.

cards.question: If judgment begins with God's family, what does Peter ask next?

answers.text: What awaits those who disobey the gospel
How long the judgment will last
Who will stand as the judge

cards.text: Then Peter quotes Proverbs 11:31, and friend, I read it once, put the dough down, and read it AGAIN with both eyebrows up: "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?"
So then, friend. I'm leaning in like it's the last ten seconds on my oven timer, because here comes Peter's word for everyone who suffers according to God's will.

cards.question: What does Peter say those who suffer according to God's will should do with their souls?

answers.text: Entrust them to their faithful Creator

cards.question: Peter says those who suffer according to God's will should stop doing good until the trial is over.
